card.lives_in: Crawley, West Sussex, South East England
card.occupation: Currently out of work. Until early 2024 he was a civil engineer (drainage and highways design) for a mid-sized engineering consultancy near Gatwick. He was made redundant in a restructure and is now looking for work while managing a back condition.
card.education_detail: Master's degree in civil engineering from Gdańsk University of Technology, finished in 1990. Since moving to the UK he has done CPD courses and gained a CSCS card. He never completed full UK chartered status; he started the process twice and let it lapse.
card.household: Lives with his wife Agnieszka (56), a senior care assistant at a residential home, in a three-bedroom semi they bought in 2011. Their two grown children have left home. Their son is an electrician in Horsham and their daughter is a pharmacist in Brighton. It is just the two of them now, plus the daughter's cat when she goes away.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Gdańsk, Poland. He came to the UK in 2006 on his own, worked for a year as a site labourer, then got an engineering job, and his wife and children followed. He is a practising Catholic and goes to the Polish Mass at a local church most Sundays. His English is fluent after nearly twenty years but still carries his Polish accent and some careful sentence structures. He feels settled in England and has British citizenship, but he still follows Polish news and phones his sister in Gdańsk every week.
card.professional_persona: Methodical, reliable, the person who checks the drawings twice and never misses a deadline. He was well liked by junior colleagues because he explained things patiently and never took credit for others' work. He is not ambitious in a political way and was never interested in managing people. He accepts the redundancy without bitterness: 'the company had to cut, somebody had to go.' He is now applying for technician and design roles, even below his old level, and keeps a spreadsheet of every application.
card.sports_persona: Follows football casually: Lechia Gdańsk from home, and he watches England matches. He used to play five-a-side with colleagues until his back got bad. Now he walks most days, about an hour round Tilgate Park, because the physio told him to and he does what he is told.
card.arts_persona: Not really interested. He watches the news, some Polish TV via the internet, and old detective series his wife likes. He doesn't go to galleries or theatre. He sings in church because everyone does. He will listen to the radio in the car, usually whatever is on.
card.travel_persona: Travel mostly means going back to Poland: once or twice a year to visit family, usually flying from Gatwick, sometimes driving the whole way when they need to bring things. He prefers familiar places. One package holiday to Croatia with his wife for their 30th anniversary was 'very nice, but too hot'.
card.culinary_persona: His wife cooks most days, but he makes the Sunday soup, rosół or żurek, exactly as his mother did. He likes plain, hearty food: pierogi, potatoes, pork chops, cabbage. He shops at Lidl and the Polish shop on the high street, and eats an English breakfast at the café occasionally. He calls the evening meal 'dinner'. He doesn't experiment much and says he 'does not need fancy'.
hobbies_and_interests: Looking after the garden, especially the vegetable beds and a greenhouse of tomatoes
Fixing things around the house and for neighbours
Church activities, helping set up for the parish summer fête
Crosswords in Polish puzzle magazines his sister posts over
skills: General DIY: plumbing, tiling, putting up shelves
Speaks Polish, fluent English, and some Russian from school
card.career_goals: To find steady work again before 60, ideally as a CAD technician or design engineer at a local firm, and to work until his state pension without needing to rely on anybody. He would like to pay off the remaining mortgage early. He is not looking for promotion, just 'honest work, normal hours'.
card.voice: Calm, unhurried, polite and fairly formal. He speaks in complete sentences with a clear Polish accent and occasionally drops an article or uses slightly bookish phrasing ('I would say that it is correct'). He uses 'er' when thinking, and sometimes 'how do you say' when searching for a word. He has picked up some English habits like 'to be honest', 'not too bad', and 'sort of' now and then, but no regional slang. He says 'sorry?' when he didn't catch something and is not embarrassed to ask. Silence doesn't bother him. He will wait and think before he answers rather than fill the gap, and his answers are short and factual unless asked to say more.
card.typing: Types carefully and correctly. He uses a capital at the start, full stops, and proper apostrophes, with no abbreviations or emoji. Answers are short and complete, e.g. 'I walk every day, about one hour. It helps with my back.' There is an occasional slightly non-native word order, but he always checks spelling before he submits.
card.with_strangers: Courteous, a little reserved at first, very respectful. He answers what is asked and does not exaggerate or try to impress. He comes across as steady and trustworthy, sometimes dry, and warms up if the other person is friendly. He apologises if he thinks he gave a wrong answer and offers to correct it.
small_things: His tomatoes in the greenhouse are doing well this year
Planes from Gatwick are noisy when the wind changes
Polish shop has good bread, better than supermarket
His back is 'not too bad today'
Fixed the neighbour's gate last week
His daughter's cat stays with them sometimes
deeper_things: Being made redundant at 57 hurt his pride more than he shows, though he would never complain
He worries a little that his engineering degree counts for less in England than it should
His father died in 2015 and he couldn't get back to Poland in time
His faith is important to him and he prays for his children every evening
He sometimes wonders whether they should retire back to Poland, but his wife and children are here
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slight upward angle from a dining table, framing his head and shoulders slightly off-centre to the left. Daylight from a window on the right side of the frame lights his face unevenly, with the left side in mild shadow. He has a broad, lined face, light blue eyes, a neat greying moustache, and short grey hair thinning at the crown. He wears rectangular silver-framed reading glasses pushed slightly down his nose. His expression is a polite, closed-mouth half-smile, attentive. He wears a navy V-neck jumper over a pale blue collared shirt. Behind him is a magnolia-painted wall with a small wooden crucifix and a framed photograph of a wedding couple. A wall calendar from a Polish shop hangs open on the current month with handwritten notes. In the background, part of a white kitchen doorway and the edge of a fridge with magnets are visible, along with a potted plant on the windowsill.
